title: Critical two-sided graph commutator seminorm is not onsite-stable
question: Does the canonical critical two-sided K^(-1/2)-damped q/p commutator seminorm satisfy a frequency-uniform onsite one-step bound?

candidate_topology.stability_target: L_K(alpha_t(A)) <= (1+C|t|) L_K(A) with C independent of Weyl frequency a
candidate_topology.status_before: OPEN as a specific non-Leibniz candidate; broader analytic/Frechet and state-weighted topologies remain open

imported_exact_lower_bound.uniformity: B_tau is finite and independent of a

new_deduction.weyl_initial_bound: [q_0,W_a]=a W_a and [p_nu,W_a]=0, so K>=1 and Weyl unitarity give L_K(W_a)<=2|a|
new_deduction.slope: For tau with G tau>2, the lower slope G tau exceeds the upper initial slope 2
new_deduction.difference: (G tau-2)a-B_tau-2 C tau/a is positive for all sufficiently large a
new_deduction.verdict: the displayed critical graph seminorm cannot obey the stated frequency-uniform onsite one-step bound

scope.closed: an exact route-level obstruction for this canonical K^(-1/2)-damped commutator seminorm
scope.open: non-Leibniz analytic/Frechet scales with frequency profiles, state-weighted topologies, direct projected-Duhamel locality, common alpha, KMS, ground/gap, continuum and Pre-A

no_overclaim: The imported lower bound is the analytic authority. This package only combines it with the exact Weyl commutator and K>=1 norm bound; it does not prove a global no-go for non-Leibniz, analytic/Frechet or state-weighted dynamics, and it does not close any QFT thermodynamic or TECT production gate.
